title: Their endings: choosing -nsa or -nsä
summary: Choose the third-person suffix vowel from back, front, and neutral-only noun bases.
objectives: Choose the third-person suffix vowel from back, front, and neutral-only noun bases.
Apply this rule with the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Vowel harmony chooses the vowel in the third-person ending. A noun containing back a, o, or u uses -nsa: auto → autonsa, kirja → kirjansa.
A noun with front ä, ö, or y and no back vowel uses -nsä: kynä → kynänsä, tyyny → tyynynsä. Neutral e and i do not change an existing back/front choice.
A noun containing only neutral e/i uses the front ending: peli → pelinsä. Look at the noun, not the owner pronoun or the number of owners.
In each form retain heidän; it identifies the owner. Keep the noun base unchanged for these regular singular forms.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Complete “their cat”: heidän kissans___. Write only a or ä. Use kissa (“cat”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Heidän selects -nsa: kissa + -nsa = kissansa. Back a/o/u chooses -nsa; front vowels or only e/i choose -nsä.
